raw_response:
I am already old, so I do not toss things around much now. On my 8.7 mu, I still do the wheat and maize rotation the same way as most people here. That land feeds us and gives us cash, so I do not dare leave it idle or try strange things. I cannot read much, so I look at what my own field did before and what the neighbors are doing. If the wheat stand looks weak, I add a bit more fertilizer. If water is short or pumping costs too much, I hold back one irrigation, but wheat still needs water at the important time. Maize goes in right after wheat harvest, very fast, no delay, otherwise you lose moisture and yield. With only two people in the house, I keep things simple and use the usual local seed and the usual fertilizer plan, not too little, because if yield drops, that loss hurts more than saving a little cash.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, use the common local improved seed people buy in the village, put fertilizer mostly at planting, then add some urea later if the crop color is not strong. I will water about three times if the year is normal: once after sowing or at overwintering if dry, once around jointing, and once around grain filling if needed. For maize, I will plant right after cutting wheat in June. There is no time for fine tillage, so I will clear the straw and do quick land preparation, same as usual. Maize I water less, maybe once or twice depending on rain. I use herbicide and maybe insecticide if I see pest pressure, but I do not spray for nothing. I am not chasing the biggest yield, just a steady harvest without spending beyond what this small household can carry.
